title: KV shadow-write cascade causing intermittent GPU OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private - patch and customer escalations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Multiple tier-1 customers reported sustained GPU OOM cascades over 2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-09. Incidents affected Hosted API, several Dedicated clusters, and a Private on-prem deployment. Symptoms: progressive increase in per-session device memory followed by hard OOMs; repros showed KV cache entries with unexpected size deltas and torn metadata leading to allocation spikes. This ticket tracks the immediate hotfix, rollout, communications, and follow-up engineering work to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Load test harness that simulates concurrent chat requests with long-history prefix (avg 1024 tokens) mixed with short queries
2) Enable KV cache with prefix caching and aggressive session pinning (dedicated config used by impacted customers),
3) Inject race via toggling concurrent session eviction and async journal flush (test harness toggles eviction window at high frequency),
4) Observe KV index entries with non-monotonic size fields and an increase in live tensor arena allocations leading to OOMs within 10-30 minutes under sustained load
impact_summary: Production degradation for 4 enterprise customers (2 Hosted tenants, 2 Dedicated clusters) and 1 Private customer. Several 5xx errors and degraded throughput; customer SLOs missed. Impact visible as step increases in memory utilization on GPUs and elevated OOM counts in runtime logs. One Dedicated customer opened an SLA escalation (account-level).
root_cause_summary: Race condition between async KV write/journal compaction and the eviction/allocator path produced partially-serialized KV index records. These 'shadow writes' left the slab allocator with inconsistent object size metadata which caused the arena to fragment and overcommit GPU memory when reconstructing KV entries, triggering hard OOMs. Contributing factors: (a) compact-on-write path did not take the same allocator fence as the main write path, (b) eviction thrashing increased allocation churn, and (c) our telemetry lacked a tight correlation between KV index metadata anomalies and slab fragmentation metrics.
mitigations: 1) Emergency rollback of compact-on-write change on hosted canary clusters (rolled back 2026-03-09 04:30 UTC) to stop new corrupt writes
2) Throttle aggressive eviction policies for affected Dedicated clusters and instruct customers to apply temporary rate caps (customer-facing runbook distributed),
3) Force journal compaction to run synchronously on Private customer's cluster as a temporary corrective step,
4) Deploy runtime flag 'kv_write_atomic=true' that enforces allocator fencing around KV write + compaction (hotfix PR linked below)
proposed_fix_summary: Introduce an atomic KV write/compact transaction boundary in the runtime: take allocator fence + journal lock around write and compaction paths, add a per-session write-seq monotonic tag and validity checksum to index records to detect torn writes on read. The hotfix also reorders compaction to produce stable index snapshots and adds a repair path that rejects and remaps corrupted index entries rather than attempting to reconstruct with stale size metadata.
rollout_plan: Canary: Deploy hotfix to internal canary cluster + 2 low-risk hosted regions; monitor for 6 hours (safety gates: no increase in 5xx, stable GPU allocation curves).
Stage: Expand to 25% of hosted traffic and 1 Dedicated staging customer; watch memory/p95 latency and kvcache-checksum alert rate for 24 hours.
Full: Ramp to 100% hosted, then schedule per-customer Dedicated upgrades with opt-in during maintenance windows. Private customers to receive patch artifacts and guided upgrade instructions.
Rollback plan: Feature-flag off 'kv_write_atomic' and revert to previous runtime build; keep throttles in place until root-cause verified fixed.
test_plan: Add synthetic workload in e2e harness that reproduces race (eviction+async-journal toggle) as an automated nightly regression test;
Unit tests for allocator fence around both write and compact code paths;
Fuzz index record serialization/deserialization to catch torn writes;
Load test on canary with long-history prefixes and monitored fragmentation metrics to validate no memory spike under heavy churn
customer_communications: 2026-03-09: Initial outage notification sent to impacted customers with mitigation steps and ETA for hotfix
2026-03-10: Follow-up with Dedicated customers offering maintenance windows and temporary throttles
Private customer: on-call runbook provided and synchronous compaction completed under engineering guidance
postmortem_actions: 1) Ship runtime-1.19 with atomic KV write and index checksum (post-rollback validation),
2) Instrument new telemetry: correlate index-checksum failures with slab fragmentation metrics and GPU allocation deltas,
3) Create ops runbook for rapid per-tenant throttle and compaction remediation,
4) Revisit eviction policy defaults and introduce a backoff to prevent thrash under heavy prefix caching workloads
notes: Incident call 2026-03-09 05:00 UTC notes: engineering, SRE, and SE on the call. Decided immediate rollback where possible and deploy hotfix to canaries.
